question: Why does attributing difference to time fail whether time or another cause produces it?
premises: If time produces difference, the account falls into infinite regress.
If another cause produces difference through mutual dependence, the same regress follows.
Conditioned difference is not ultimately real or substantial.
inference: Difference cannot establish time as a real independent principle.
plain_english: Whether difference is produced by time itself or by something else through mutual dependence, the result is infinite regress; and since such conditioned difference is unreal and unsubstantial, it cannot establish time as truly real.
